record.paper_title: Recent Theoretical Advances and Open Problems in Nuclear Cluster Physics
record.original_question: Which neutron-rich nuclei with valence neutrons, such as carbon-13, carbon-14, and beryllium isotopes, contain Hoyle-like α-cluster gas states, and how do extra neutrons modify the α-cluster structure relative to self-conjugate nuclei with equal neutron and proton numbers?

evidence.quote: So far, we only considered selfconjugate nuclei with N =Z. However, α clustering should survive adding some extra neutrons. For example is there some sign of a Hoyle like state in 13C or 14C, etc. ?

Further important studies concern α clustering in nuclei with valence neutrons. It is very likel y that such states exist, e.g., in 13C, 14C, etc. The works we cite show that the situation may be more co mplex as assumed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In nuclear cluster physics, the Hoyle state is the second 0⁺ excited state of ¹²C near 7.65 MeV above the ground state, and is interpreted as a dilute, weakly interacting gas-like (Bose–Einstein-condensate-like) configuration of three α particles. Such configurations have so far been studied principally in self-conjugate nuclei with equal neutron and proton numbers N = Z (e.g., ⁸Be, ¹²C, ¹⁶O, ²⁰Ne, …), where they are conjectured to appear near the Nα breakup threshold.

Consider neutron-rich nuclei that can be modeled as an α-cluster core surrounded by additional valence neutrons, in particular the carbon isotopes ¹³C (3α + n) and ¹⁴C (3α + 2n), and the beryllium isotopes (e.g., 2α + xn systems such as ⁹Be, ¹⁰Be, ¹¹Be, ¹²Be).

Problem:

(a) Determine which of these neutron-rich nuclei support Hoyle-like α-cluster gas states, i.e., low-density excited 0⁺ (or analogous Jᵖ) states near the multi-α + xn breakup threshold whose intrinsic structure is well approximated by a dilute condensate of α particles together with valence neutrons in single-particle (molecular-orbital or covalent) configurations.

(b) Quantify how the presence of the extra valence neutrons modifies the α-cluster structure relative to the corresponding N = Z Hoyle-like state, addressing the binding energy and excitation energy of such states relative to the multi-α threshold, the spatial extent and density profile of the α-cluster core, the rotational/vibrational band structure built upon these states, and the role of the valence neutrons (covalent "molecular" binding versus mean-field-like delocalization) in stabilizing or destabilizing the α gas configuration.

Provide a theoretical characterization of these Hoyle-like states with valence neutrons and identify experimental signatures that would distinguish them from non-clusterized excited states.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial theoretical and experimental progress has been made on α-clustering in neutron-rich carbon and beryllium isotopes (e.g., molecular-orbital structures in ⁹⁻¹²Be, linear-chain and clustered states in ¹³C and ¹⁴C), and reviews from 2022–2024 describe valence neutrons as playing a covalent "glue" role that stabilizes α-cluster configurations. However, a definitive identification of true Hoyle-analog (dilute α-condensate-like) states in ¹³C, ¹⁴C, and beryllium isotopes — and a complete quantification of how valence neutrons modify the α-gas structure compared with N = Z Hoyle states — is still under active investigation, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Clustering and molecular states in neutron rich nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Cluster states consisting of three alpha particles are stabilized by covalent valence neutrons; molecular-like 3α+xn states are observed in carbon isotopes, e.g., ¹³C→n+α+α+α and ¹⁴C→α+α+α+n+n.
status_evidence.claim: Alpha-cluster states with valence neutrons exist in ¹³C and ¹⁴C, with valence neutrons playing a covalent role; structural details are still being mapped.

status_evidence.title: 1/2⁻ α cluster resonances of ¹³C
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) study of 1/2⁻ α-cluster resonances in ¹³C using analytic continuation in the coupling constant.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent theoretical work continues to investigate α-cluster resonances in ¹³C, indicating the question is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Clustering in nuclei: progress and perspectives
status_evidence.snippet: 2024 review describing ongoing progress on α clustering and Hoyle-like states, including in neutron-rich systems.
status_evidence.claim: A 2024 review treats Hoyle-like states with valence neutrons as an active and only partially resolved research direction.
